subject: AWS PO: pricing signal & approver lattice for 12-month pilot
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Samuels <ava.samuels@altitude-health.com>, procurement@altitude-health.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: AWS PO: pricing signal & approver lattice for 12-month pilot

Hi Ava / Altitude procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited by the fit for your care-coordination workload. We discussed using an AWS Marketplace private offer for a 12-month pilot and I wanted to surface the recommended pricing/approver approach so you can preview what we'll submit to AWS.

High-level proposal (attached: RDW_PO_pricing_model_v3.pdf):
- Offer A (12-month pilot): metered consumption + 20% marketplace discount, onboarding credit of $15k.
- Offer B (12-month committed spend): $X committed annual equivalent, 30% marketplace discount, waived setup fee.

Why two signals: buyers often prefer the lower-commitment meter for pilots; the committed SKU speeds legal/finance approval for teams ready to buy. We can expose both SKUs in the private offer and programmatically fallback during activation.

Approver lattice note: from prior private-offer activations we expect procurement -> IT security -> CFO (for any commit > $250k) -> cloud PM for activation scheduling. Can you confirm who needs to sign on your side? If CFO signoff is required we'll include a line item that shows annualized savings to shorten approval cycles.

Request / next steps:
1) Can you share your internal approval path (names/roles) so we can tailor the offer and escalation notes for AWS?
2) Which evidence matters most (SOC 2, data residency, SLA)? We have a short evidence pack I can send immediately.
3) Are you available Wed 11/4 at 10am PT for a 30-minute procurement handoff call?

Attaching the pricing model and a short SOC2-summary.pdf.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
AE, Marketplace & Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: RDW_PO_pricing_model_v3.pdf (pdf), SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful.

Quick answers: procurement will route to CFO for any commitment over $200k (our internal threshold), and legal will want the standard evidence pack (SOC2 + encryption in transit at minimum). IT security will validate technical controls and may ask for a short runbook for onboarding.

I can make the 11/4 10am PT call — please send a calendar invite. Also, can you include a one-page activation checklist we can circulate to our cloud PM ahead of the call? That'll speed the security review.

Ava Samuels
Head of Procurement, Altitude Health

- Draft a buyer-facing one-pager activation checklist and the short runbook for IT security (I attached a draft activation-checklist.xlsx).
- Prepare evidence bundle for legal (SOC2-summary.pdf + DocSend link).
- Pricing signoff: Vanessa, can we approve the 20%/30% bands as the default marketplace signals? If customer needs deeper discount we should route to Neha for an exception.

Vanessa — highlight: if CFO involvement is expected, include the annualized cost-savings calculation in the offer description to accelerate their finance review.

Marcus
